name: a_macro_secondary
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Secondary macro & officials.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Regional Fed surveys (Dallas, Richmond, Kansas City, Empire, Philly) actual vs prior; every Fed governor/president speech with verbatim quotes; Treasury and White House economic appointments; fiscal watchdog reports (CBO, CRFB) on debt and rates; foreign CEOs of US-listed companies commenting on trade/export controls.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Macro / Commodities / Calendar

- October Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index fell to **+20.9** in October from **+37.8** in September; new orders declined to **4.3** from **29.2**, shipments to **15.3** from **27.7**, and prices paid to **43.2** from **48.6**. (InvestingLive, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not stated)
- The Philadelphia Fed’s six-month index declined to **33.0** in October from **52.9** in September. (InvestingLive, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not stated)
- The Congressional Budget Office estimated a **$1.993 trillion** federal deficit, while CNBC reported the deficit was expected to equal approximately **6.0%–6.2% of GDP**; CBO’s 10-year Treasury assumption was **4.3%**, versus a reported market yield of **5.3%**. (CNBC, Oct 15, 2026, 05:30 ET)
- CBO estimated that rates averaging **0.5 percentage point** above its expectations would add **$1.9 trillion** to cumulative 10-year deficits, while rates **1.5 percentage points** higher would add approximately **$6 trillion**. (CNBC, Oct 15, 2026, 05:30 ET)
- The 10-year Treasury yield closed at **5.19%** on Wednesday, after rising **123 basis points** from the end of February; mortgage rates were reported near **7.5%**. (CNBC, Oct 15, 2026, 05:30 ET)
- Treasury counselor **David Zervos**, described as newly appointed, said the IMF should examine its forecasting record before criticizing U.S. fiscal policy; IMF Managing Director **Kristalina Georgieva** said economic growth alone would not reduce U.S. debt quickly enough and called for fiscal measures. (CNBC, Oct 15, 2026, 08:40 ET)
- U.S. federal debt exceeded **$40 trillion**, while 10-year Treasury yields remained above **5%**. (CNBC, Oct 15, 2026, 08:40 ET)
- Federal Reserve Governor **Christopher Waller** said rising long-term Treasury yields were restraining demand in interest-rate-sensitive sectors including housing and automobiles. (Ground News/Reuters, Oct 15, 2026; original Reuters item dated Oct 13, publication time not stated)
- Waller said U.S. inflation expectations remained **“well anchored”** and attributed higher Treasury yields to stronger growth, artificial-intelligence investment, and debt dynamics rather than higher inflation expectations. (Ground News/Reuters, Oct 15, 2026; original Reuters item dated Oct 13, publication time not stated)
- Federal Reserve Chair **Kevin Warsh** was scheduled to speak in Bangkok on Friday morning at the IMF–World Bank annual meeting, after **23:00 ET** on Thursday, with an interview by IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva; the event was described as the last Fed-official speech before the blackout period beginning Saturday. (NBC News, Oct 15, 2026, 16:28 ET)
- Warsh said the 10-year Treasury was affected by a **“competition for capital”** and described it as the **“risk-free asset upon which every price of virtually every asset in the world is related to.”** (NBC News, Oct 15, 2026, 16:28 ET)
- Warsh said geopolitical factors and economic strength were driving Treasury yields; the article reported market expectations for a potential October rate increase following two inflation reports. (NBC News, Oct 15, 2026, 16:28 ET)
- Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** said the United States should target a deficit below **4% of GDP** by the end of President Donald Trump’s term and said, **“My view is that we’ve got this mountain of debt, and we have to grow our way out of it.”** (CNBC, Oct 15, 2026, 05:30 ET)
- The Richmond Fed’s October Beige Book update said Fifth District economic activity grew at a **moderate** pace, manufacturing activity was **flat**, and price growth remained **moderate** year over year. (Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, Oct 14, 2026; update time not stated)
